They were translated from English by Google Translate's document translation (five files uploaded by the founder) and checked by script; person names keep their English transliteration; titles of sources are left as published; the frozen Qur'an passage records are untouched. About 750 texts the checks refused are still missing. Machine translation, not read by a human.
- **The validator and the tests are given 8 GB of memory (`.npmrc`).** They read every page and record into memory, about 7 GB now, and the validator stopped with "heap out of memory" at Node's default of about 4 GB once the Spanish texts were added.
- **Every exhibit and trail now has its title, summary and steps in Urdu, French and Spanish (318 records).** A trail such as «Islam in Thirty Minutes» showed its title in Arabic and its twelve steps in English to an Urdu, French or Spanish reader, because that text lives in the record and had Arabic and English only (19 exhibits also had Urdu). 11,524 short texts were added: translated from English by Google Translate's document translation (the founder uploaded the file by hand), checked by script, and 19 written by Claude where the machine left a name in Latin letters or the English field itself held Arabic. Blessing formulas the machine added after «the Prophet» in Urdu were taken out, as the museum types none. Machine translation, not read by a human. Tool: `scripts/local-mt/data_strings.py`.
- **The museum's pages on single Qur'an verses are now in Spanish and French: 6,350 pages in each language.** They hold the museum's own prose about a verse (its place in the surah and, for about 1,700 verses, a summary of al-Tabari's commentary); the verse text itself stays in Arabic, from the frozen Tanzil file. 12,687 pages were translated from English by Google Translate's document translation, the 13 that failed the automatic checks by a Claude agent. Machine translation, checked by script, not read by a human.
- **The last very long French records are translated**: ten by Google Translate's document translation and four in consecutive parts by Claude agents, one of them begun by Gemini; each file names its translators.

### Changed
- **New content must come in all five languages, whatever its kind (founder rule, 20 November 2026; `AGENTS.md`, `docs/language.md`).** The standing rule asked for Arabic, English, Urdu, French and Spanish on prose and interface strings. It now also names the titles, summaries and every other language block inside data records, the site datasets, the vocabulary files and text written in pages: a new record, field or dataset that lacks one of the five is not finished. Older content stays valid and is being filled.
- **Every pull request now goes to `main`; the Spanish release branch is retired (founder's instruction, 19 November 2026).** The Spanish and French translation work was collected on `release/spanish`. It is now merged into `main`, and the lane document, the translation how-to and the shipping scripts of the lane (`scripts/local-mt/ship_gt.sh`, `ship.sh`) raise against `main` only.
- **How bulk translation is done is written down (`docs/engineering/63-translation-by-document-files.md`, pointer in `AGENTS.md` and the Spanish lane document).** One English Word file per round goes through Google Translate's document translation, once for Spanish and once for French; link labels travel as Word hyperlinks and citations as 10-digit numbers, which kept 96–100% of records intact where text markers kept 11–63%. The page records the limits found (about 1.2 million words per file; a usage limit after about fifteen files) and that Arabic as the source was tested and not adopted.
- **Translation moves from the local model to Google Translate documents (founder's instruction, 19 November 2026).** A pilot showed that a plain-text Word file of about one megabyte (1,644 concept records, about 494,000 English words) is translated by translate.google.com in under a minute, where the local model needs more than a day. `scripts/local-mt/import_gt.py` splits the downloaded file back into records, restores citations and link ids, and applies the same checks as the local translator; 1,588 Spanish and 1,282 French records from the pilot passed and are in, each naming Google Translate in its `translators` and `provenance`. Records whose citation or link markers Google altered (about 3% in Spanish, 22% in French) were not imported. The local model threads are stopped. Nobody has read these translations.
- **The site build now clears unused tools off the build machine before it starts.** GitHub's build machine is documented with 14 GB of disk, and a build of five languages writes more than that; the build of 18 November on the Spanish release branch most likely stopped for want of disk, though that run printed no reading that proves it. The machine ships with tools this build never uses (the Android SDK, .NET, Haskell, CodeQL, Swift, Docker images). A new first step removes them and prints the free disk before and after. How much it frees is not yet measured: the next build's log will show it. The site itself is unchanged.
- **The site build now reports the build machine's free disk and memory while it runs.** The build of 18 November on the Spanish release branch stopped after two hours because GitHub lost contact with the machine. Its log simply stops while pages are being written, about 462,000 pages in, with no error message, so nobody could tell whether memory or disk had run out. (An earlier wording of this note said the run left no log; that was wrong, and is corrected here.) The build step now prints both before it starts and every five minutes, and raises a warning on the run page when under 4 GB of disk or 1 GB of memory is left. It only reads; the build itself is unchanged.
- **Translation now runs on a local model on the founder's Mac (from wave 11).** Spanish and French prose are translated from English by TranslateGemma 27B, served locally with Ollama, under `scripts/local-mt/` (a translator that protects citations, link ids and markers and checks every record against its English source, and a supervisor that restarts it). Claude manages the queue, the checks and the merges and no longer writes the translations. The local drafts are freer than the earlier ones and are labelled with the model's name on every record; nobody has read them.
### Data
- **First Spanish prose: 34,598 records (`content/es/`, branch `release/spanish`).** Every eligible record of the canon's top two tiers and 792 object and building records, outside the sacred classes — people such as Umm Salama, al-Nawawi, al-Tabari, Rumi and Mansa Musa, places such as Granada, Qayrawan, Bukhara and Delhi, buildings such as the Dome of the Rock and al-Azhar, events, works, concepts and periods — now have their full prose in Spanish, translated from the English by AI agents and checked mechanically against it (same links, citations, headings and paragraphs; no typed honorific). No human has read them. About 33,400 prose files are still English under `/es/`, and every label and summary, and the education, kids and tour datasets are still not in Spanish.

### Fixed
- **French and Spanish are now named wherever the site listed its languages by hand.** Four places still knew only Arabic, English and Urdu, or only Arabic and English: the redirect that takes a renamed record's old address to its new one (it did nothing under `/fr/` and `/es/`), `robots.txt` (the rule that keeps crawlers from fetching one copy of the graph explorer per record), the list of changed pages sent to search engines after a production deploy (it also left out Urdu), and `llms.txt`, which said the museum is published in Arabic and English. The sitemap already listed all five. Search synonyms still exist for Arabic and English only; Urdu, French and Spanish have none yet.
- **The build works again on the Spanish release branch: the compiled graph had grown too large to be read in one piece.** The graph file that every build step reads (`.cache/graph.json`) reached 549 MB on 19 November 2026 with five languages of prose, and Node cannot read a file larger than about 512 MB as one text. Validation, the unit tests and the site build all stopped there with the same error. The file is unchanged; it is now read and written a part at a time (`scripts/lib/graph-file.mjs`), by the site build and by the 20 scripts that used it, and the real file reads back to the same bytes.
- **French pages no longer stop the site build.** The table of other prophets' names had no French entry, so a French page that mentioned the Prophet made the build fail (`/fr/event/hijra/`). The French and Spanish tables are both present now.
- **Spanish prose reads left to right and keeps its section roles.** The entity page, the place map and several components treated every language but English as right-to-left (fix taken unchanged from the French lane), and the Spanish headings of the Brief, young-visitors, scholars and reading-level sections are registered. The validator's "Sunni entry first" rule recognises the Spanish label.
- **Pages that read the education, kids, tour and card datasets no longer break in French and Spanish.** Those datasets exist in Arabic, English and Urdu only; a page such as `/fr/shabab/detective/` read a French field that was not there and stopped the build. The loaders now fill a missing French or Spanish field from English, then Arabic, when the data is read, so the page shows the English text until the translation lands.
- **The Time Browser has its data in French and Spanish.** Its generator wrote the per-language files for Arabic, English and Urdu only, which stopped the build at the Time Browser's stop pages.
- **The kids' reader is built only where its text exists.** A record flagged for the kids' reader got a reader page, and links to it, in every language that had any prose for it; in French that page had no Explorers text and stopped the build, and in Spanish the links led nowhere. The page and its links now exist only where the record's prose in that language has the Explorers section.

- French leveled reading fixed for five records that had two "Pour les Petits" sections (al-dawa-al-sirriyya, abu-sufyan-ibn-harb, abu-talib, abu-ubayda-ibn-al-jarrah, al-aqra-ibn-habis): the first section is kept, the second dropped (still in git history). Six "Pour les Explorateurs" sections (kaaba, battle-of-yamama, abd-allah-ibn-amir, al-bara-ibn-azib, al-qadir-billah, al-qaim-billah) trimmed to 160 words or fewer, removing secondary details only.

### Tests
- **The site check reads a partly translated strings file.** `scripts/check-site.ts` crashed on a language whose `i18n` file lacks a section (French today); it now falls back to the English string, as the pages do.
- **The Qur'an passage files are back to their frozen content (branch `release/spanish`).** A corpus-wide change on `main` (commit `7d509c17a5`) had inserted direction marks around parentheses in 3,528 of the 6,394 Qur'an passage files: in the Urdu translation text (3,522 values) and in relation notes (21). The Arabic Qur'an text, the search text and the English translation were not touched. On the founder's instruction the 3,528 files are restored to what they were before that commit, and the validator no longer applies the parenthesis rule to the frozen passage files. Until the page renderer isolates them, parentheses in the Urdu translation on passage pages may be drawn the wrong way round.
- **The accessible books step runs in five languages.** `scripts/a11y-books.ts` kept one list per language for four of the five and crashed on Spanish at the very end of the first full build of `release/spanish` (after 460,598 pages had been built and checked with 0 errors). French and Spanish now also go through their own braille tables instead of the Arabic path. Known limit: the Spanish and French braille files lose accented letters.
- **Three tests assert the published languages again.** `pipeline.test.ts`, `tour.test.ts` and `modern.test.ts` expected French prose, French tour fields and a four-language fixture that do not exist yet, which failed the build workflow on the release branches. All 634 tests pass.

## v2.23.0 — 2026-11-17
### Added
- **The museum's own podcast feed for "Hudhud's Story Time" (the Kids' Wing story podcast).** Two static files under `/podcast/`: `feed.xml`, a complete RSS feed for Season 1 (ten English episodes told by Grandpa and Grandma, each episode linking back to the museum page its story came from, with the show's artist, Kids & Family / Stories for Kids category and owner details the podcast directories require), and `hudhud-story-time-cover.jpg`, the show's 3000×3000 cover art. The episode audio stays where it is hosted; the feed simply gives the museum a permanent, self-controlled address for Apple Podcasts, Spotify and every other directory, instead of a feed whose show details could not be completed.
- **Workflow files for the second step of the by-language trial (`main` carries the files only).** The by-language build gains a job for the parts of the site that belong to no language and a job that joins the languages' sitemaps, and there are four new deploy workflows: "Deploy shared parts" and "Deploy all parts", each for UAT and for production. GitHub offers a hand-started workflow only when its file is on `main`, so the files are here; the code they need is on the Spanish release branch, and until that branch is merged they work only when started on it. The one build and the one deploy are unchanged, and none of the new workflows has run yet.
- **Workflow files for a trial of building and publishing one language at a time (`main` carries the files only).** GitHub offers a hand-started workflow only when its file is on `main`, so the twelve files of the trial are added here: "Build islam.museum by language", the shared language deploy, and ten "Deploy `<lang>` pages" workflows (five production, five UAT). The code they need (the one-language switch in the site build and in the R2 publish) is on `release/spanish` and not on `main`, so today they work only when started on that branch, and the production ones cannot work until that code reaches `main`. The existing build and deploys are unchanged; nothing was built or deployed with the new files.
- **French learning activities:** all 20 illustrated story decks, 21 source-detective cases and 31 classroom dilemmas now include French, so learners can read the stories, weigh evidence and compare viewpoints in French. Verse references use explanatory paraphrases rather than verse translations.
- **French education topic lessons, topics 29–39:** eleven of the fifty taught topics (the Great Mosque of Córdoba through the House of Wisdom) now carry French titles, explainers, glossaries and practice questions in `edu/topics-50.yaml`, so French readers no longer fall back to English for them. Existing Arabic, English and Urdu text is unchanged; the other topic ranges are translated separately.
- **French topic lessons:** the ten lessons from Medina through Fatima al-Fihri now include French summaries, glossaries and practice questions with answer explanations. Other topic lessons are unchanged.
- **French homework search:** French classroom phrases now expand to their target labels through French synonym shards and the canon search index, instead of using English-only synonyms.
- **French dataset rollout scope:** the kids, museum-card and education-support translations are based on the separate French tour/baseline-fixtures work. The large topic lessons and recursive education activities remain untranslated; this partial rollout does not claim full French coverage.
- **French education support datasets:** age-band introductions, stamp names, seasonal packs, family activities, homework search phrases, location riddles and the approved leveled-reading record labels now include French. The large topic lessons and recursive education activities are not yet translated in this batch.
- **French museum-card datasets:** all card decks, daily prompts, the thirty-day challenge and editorial word-map titles now include French. Verse-quoting fields use clearly signalled explanatory paraphrases, not newly typed scripture; references, verification notes and age-gating are retained.
- **French topic lessons (damascus to hajj-network):** twelve of the fifty education topic lessons (Damascus, the rise of Islam, Baghdad and the Silk Roads, al-Andalus, the Mongols and after, the Five Pillars in daily life, Islamic art and architecture, the life of the Prophet, the Qur'an as a text, the Ottomans and gunpowder empires, four cities, and the Hajj network) now include French titles, summaries and glossaries. Qur'an quotations are rendered as explanatory paraphrases, not verse translations; the other topic lessons follow in separate batches.
- **French Kids’ Wing datasets:** French children’s stories and activities and teacher lesson plans now accompany the existing languages, reducing English fallbacks for French readers. Source references and existing review statuses are unchanged; the wider French dataset rollout is still in progress.

- **Umuma Browser — Motherhood in Islam (متصفح الأمومة في الإسلام, `/{lang}/umuma/`).** A new browser over the one graph listing everything the museum's sources mention about motherhood — the mother and her standing, pregnancy, childbirth, nursing and milk-kinship, the custody and raising of children, and dutifulness to parents — in the Qur'an, the two Sahihs, the Muwatta and the Sunan, the seerah books, Companion and Tabi'i reports and every harvested book, present and future. Passages are found at build time by a guarded lexicon in `scripts/umuma.ts` across six topical families (umm/haml/wilada/radaa/tarbiya/birr): bare «أم» counts only beside family vocabulary («أم القرى», «أم الكتاب» and «أمة» excluded), «حمل» counts in the pregnancy sense only beside pregnancy vocabulary (carrying/transport excluded), «ولد» the boy is out and only the birth forms count, «بر» counts only beside parent vocabulary, and verified false positives drop out by id — so a book harvested later brings its motherhood mentions automatically. Records are grouped into five corpus sections (quran, sunnah, seerah, books, curated) with topic chips; mothers on record surface the graph's own `child_of` edges to female parents — no side list. Twenty existing records tagged `umuma-browser` in place (umm, ummahat-al-muminin, rada, rada-suckling-fiqh, istilad-umm-al-walad, birr-al-walidayn, aqiqa, aqiqah, kafalat-al-yatim, tahnik, and the mothers Amina bint Wahb, Maryam, Hajar, Khadija, Fatima, Sumayya bint Khayyat, Halima al-Sa'diyya, Asiya and Fatima bint Asad) plus five new cited `concept` seeds — `umuma`, `haml`, `wilada`, `hidana`, `birr-al-umm` — each with trilingual label, summary and prose cited to the Tanzil Qur'an, the two Sahihs, the Muwatta, Sunan Abi Dawud and the Kuwaiti Fiqh Encyclopaedia. Signature view `sig/UmumaLines.astro`: the six lines of motherhood, a disc per corpus section on each line sized by record count. `/api/v1/umuma.json`, an Explore-menu entry and landing card, trilingual ar/en/ur pages, plan `docs/plan/64-umuma-browser.md`, acceptance spec `docs/engineering/56-umuma-browser-requirements.md` (`UMUMA-R..`, original Arabic/English requirement recorded verbatim incl. the microSD/merge instructions), lane `umuma`. - Twenty-two more records of Ibn Sina's Canon, Book III (the diseases of each organ, head to foot), volume 2, printed pages 350 to 370 (pages.json indices 349 to 369): the rest of the tenth fann's fourth maqala — peripneumonia (the hot tumour of the lung), its signs and its passage into suppuration; the lung's hard, soft, pustule and water gatherings and the windpipe's tumour and wound; the pus and the filling of the chest cavity, its causes, its four outcomes, its side-signs and the sound and bad bursting, with the author's and Galen's witnessings on the amounts spat; the ulcers of chest, diaphragm, lung and windpipe — the lung ulcer being consumption — with the physicians' disagreement and Galen's ruling on what heals; the causes of the lung's ulcers; those predisposed to consumption in build, complexion, age, country and temperament and what they must shun; and the consumption's signs to the end of the maqala — then the whole of maqala 5, the treatments: the common matters (the ordered venesections, the cupping and scarification, Galen's warning on purging under severe fever, the regimen of drinks and waters by season); the pleurisy treatment (the evacuations by blood and by humour, the direction of the pain ruling venesection or purge, the feeding ladder from barley water) and its poultices, liniments, moist and dry compresses, cupping glasses and the ancients' lohochs and under-tongue pills; the non-pure phlegmatic and melancholic kinds and the water-in-lung treatment; peripneumonia's treatment; the discourse on suppuration (aiding ripening, aiding the burst, the post-burst cleansing, the fine cautery and the lancet drainage, all carried as the book's descriptions); and the chest-region ulcers' treatment — the true cure and the palliation — with the milks (women's, donkey's, goat's, mare's, cow's), the accomplished physician's milk-drinking method, the buttermilk method, and the consumptive's foods. Each is a trilingual concept in the Medicine Browser cited to the printed page; recipes, doses, drug and plant names, decoctions, electuaries, pills, lohochs, draughts, juices, oils, salves, cerates, poultices, fumigations, clysters, suppositories and food prescriptions are not reproduced; the animal- and human-derived lines (women's milk suckled from the breast, donkey, goat, mare, cow and sheep milks, the fox's lung, the cow and goat kidney fats, the mountain-cow dung, the tar spoonful, the trotters, the plucked-claw crabs) are kept as labelled listings for the founder; the toxic and stupefying lines (the arsenic fumigations, the stupefying admixtures, the poppy-descended syrup and the under-tongue pills) are named only as kinds; the sayings and reports (Galen, Hippocrates, Yusuf al-Sahir, the accomplished physicians' milk method, the ancients' vs the moderns' practice, the author's own witnessings and the tried-remedy lines) are carried as the book's attributions and labelled; and the hand-works (the red-clay cloth pus-finder, the fine cautery piercing the chest, the lancet drainage, the pus-drawing instrument, the uvula's cutting, the postures, the chair-shaking, the heated-stone milk cooking, the hot iron in the buttermilk) are carried as the book's descriptions, not as procedures.
- Wa Nalqa al-Ahibba, Amr Khaled (lecture series, Assabile archive): episode 27 added, the first of the Aisha bint Abi Bakr episodes — the introduction to Aisha as the speaker presents her: the repeated rule verse, the wives' quiz and the book list with a new al-Bouti title; her place as the Prophet's beloved, the only virgin he married on the speaker's word, daughter of Abu Bakr; the house of Abu Bakr (Qutayla mother of Asma and Abdullah, Umm Ruman mother of Aisha and Abd al-Rahman, the half-sisters); Umm Ruman's emigration and death after the ifk incident and the Prophet praying over her and descending into her grave; Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakr's late conversion after fighting at Badr and Uhud; the screen's numbers (born year five of the mission, betrothed at seven, married at nine, widowed at eighteen, dead on 17 Ramadan 57 AH aged sixty-six, the transcript contradicting itself at points); Khawla bint Hakim's visit to Umm Ruman; Abu Bakr's hesitation because al-Mut'im ibn Adi's son Jubayr had asked for her; the lesson on keeping one's word and on steady character toward the disbeliever; al-Mut'im's wife speaking first and releasing Abu Bakr; the Prophet's betrothal; the audience's mother-in-law comment; the woman's question about the nine-year age and the whole answer session (early maturity in hot climates, environment and custom, the earlier betrothal, examples of Hafsa, Safiyya and Amina, the doubt's recentness, a quoted English Orientalist via Aisha Abd al-Rahman's book, the speaker's own caution that girls today must not imitate the age); the why-he-married-her section (a young long-lived transmitter of the Prophet's private life, her narrated questions and stories, the four caliphs' marriage ties, Muhammad the man versus Muhammad the messenger, and the dream hadith he attributes to al-Bukhari); in Arabic, English and Urdu drafts, each statement cited to the recording by timestamp, the speaker's and audience's contested answers about her age placed under perspectives and never asserted by the museum, the audience's statements attributed to their speakers, and the museum's readings of garbled names and the repetition loops listed in the 'left out' sections; machine transcript, not listened to.

Machine translation from the English pivot, placeholders and links unchanged.
### Changed
- The virtual tour now includes French exhibit labels, gallery descriptions and journey narration. The French Farewell Pilgrimage description specifies that it was the Prophet’s only hajj.
### Fixed
- **French reading and navigation (PR #7416).** French pages read left to right; the reading-level headings and brief, young-visitor and scholarly sections are recognized in French. The translation queue also finds Arabic-only sacred records. Object translations were checked against the museum’s Arabic prose and catalogue data to correct inherited English-pivot errors without silently rewriting Arabic-agreeing source conflicts.
- **French kids' reader no longer stops the site build.** The leveled-reading headings now have their French forms (“Pour les Petits”, “Pour les Explorateurs”, “Pour les Chercheurs”) in `edu/levels.yaml`, so a French article written with them is recognised by the validator and by the kids' reader (`/fr/sighar/read/…`). Before this, the first French record flagged for children (`building/bayt-al-hikma`) made every pull request to the French release branch fail at the build step.
- **French Time Browser links no longer stop the site build.** The Time Browser's prepared record lists are now written for French as well as Arabic, English and Urdu, with French titles and summaries where a record has them, so the old per-stop addresses (`/fr/time-browser/<kind>/<slug>/`) redirect to the museum entry like the other languages. That redirect page also now declares French as left-to-right; it used to mark every language except English as right-to-left.
- **The after-build site check reads a partly translated language the way its pages do.** `scripts/check-site.ts` now takes its strings through the site's own loader, which fills a key French has not translated yet from English, so the check compares each page with the text it really shows instead of crashing on the missing French section. The embed index and not-found page checks are unchanged for Arabic, English and Urdu.
- French prose perspective labels such as “Point de vue sunnite” now satisfy the Sunni-first check, while negated forms such as “non-sunnite” do not. Validation and rendering share label parsing and accept regular spaces, non-breaking spaces and narrow non-breaking spaces before the colon. French community names and attribution verbs also participate in the existing label-before-view warning.
- **French release verification:** missing French dataset fields now have safe tour, gallery and world-page fallbacks, French prophet-name guards keep honorific rendering scoped correctly, and localized component types accept optional French fields during the rollout. The French queue imports the existing repository path helper correctly. Validate now builds the graph cache before its unit tests; regression tests cover French routes, search-index routing and the R2 sync prefix configuration.
- **A web address in Arabic or Urdu text no longer swallows the punctuation after it.** A bare address typed in a summary or article (`www.example.org` or `https://…`) now ends before «؛», «،», «؟» and «۔», the way it already ended before a Latin full stop, comma or semicolon. Before this, «…والموقع www.semerkand.tv؛» made the semicolon part of the link, so the link on the source page `wikipedia-semerkand-tv-diq` was broken and the full-site link check on `main` failed; the IslamQA listing page had the same fault with «،». Bracketed links are unchanged.
- **Arabic and Urdu parentheses now display the right way round.** About 20,400 files had plain brackets around Arabic-script text, which right-to-left pages draw turned the wrong way, such as «الخطيب (المؤلف)»: 247 Arabic and 7,052 Urdu articles, the Arabic and Urdu UI strings and about 13,100 data records. They now carry the U+2066/U+2069 isolates the rule requires, and `npm run validate` rejects a plain one in new Arabic or Urdu content. The Arabic and Urdu “approximately” date tag and the names in the art and Muslim-world data files of the site got the same fix.
- **ﷺ now appears only for Prophet Muhammad, in Arabic, English and Urdu.** The page renderer used to add it to the first «النبي» / "the Prophet" / «رسول اللہ» of every article, so «معركة النبي صموئيل», "the Prophet Daniel", «عيسى رسول الله» and a bare «النبي» on another prophet's own page carried Muhammad's mark (about fifty such marks across the site, found by rendering every article before and after). A title with another prophet named beside it is now left unmarked; the rule for new content is in `AGENTS.md`, and `npm run validate` checks that source texts keep ﷺ only beside Muhammad.
### Tests
- The reach-index test counts French Wikipedia, the graph test checks a record that already has French prose, and CI builds the graph cache before running tests.
